item.title: Modi, Trump stress keeping Strait of Hormuz open amid Iran war
item.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone on Tuesday, their first conversation since the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes against Iran on February 28. The call focused on the escalating conflict in the Middle East and the need to keep the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply — open and accessible.

"Received a call from President Trump and had a useful exchange of views on the situation in West Asia," Modi wrote on X. "India supports de-escalation and restoration of peace at the earliest. Ensuring that the Strait of Hormuz remains open, secure and accessible is essential for the whole world."

U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor confirmed the call, writing on X that the two leaders "discussed the ongoing situation in the Middle East, including the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open." A White House official confirmed the conversation but declined to comment on its substance.

item.title: US awaits Iran's response on proposed Thursday peace summit
item.description:
The United States and regional mediators are waiting on Tehran's answer to a proposed high-level peace summit that could take place as early as Thursday, even as the month-old war continues and the Pentagon prepares to send thousands more troops to the Middle East.

Two sources with knowledge of the discussions told Axios that Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey have been passing messages between Washington and Tehran, with Pakistan offering to host the talks in Islamabad. President Trump shared Pakistan's offer on Truth Social, signaling his interest in making a summit happen. If plans firm up, Vice President JD Vance is expected to represent the U.S. side, potentially facing Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, whom the White House views as its highest-level potential counterpart in Tehran.

item.title: Trump extends Iran deadline as Strait of Hormuz remains closed to shipping
item.description: Nearly four weeks after the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran, the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut to international shipping, with prediction markets, corporate leaders, and diplomats all pointing to a resolution that could take weeks or months to materialize. President Donald Trump on Monday extended by five days a deadline for Iran to reopen the waterway, citing "very good and productive conversations" — claims Tehran promptly denied.

item.title: Iran denies charging $2M for Hormuz passage after lawmaker's claim
item.description: Nearly a month into the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, Tehran has moved to assert an unprecedented degree of control over the Strait of Hormuz, with an Iranian lawmaker confirming that some vessels are being charged roughly $2 million for passage through the world's most critical oil chokepoint — even as Iran's government officially denies any such policy exists.

item.title: 15-point US ceasefire proposal for Iran war emerges
item.description: Israel's Channel 12 on Tuesday published a 15-point U.S. document reportedly being developed to halt the war with Iran, outlining sweeping demands for Tehran to dismantle its nuclear capabilities in exchange for sanctions relief. The proposal, which envisions a one-month ceasefire during which a broader framework agreement would be negotiated, comes as the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran enters its fourth week amid contradictory signals from Washington and Tehran about whether talks are even taking place.

item.title: Iran tells IMO that 'non-hostile' ships may transit Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Tuesday circulated a letter to International Maritime Organization member states declaring that "non-hostile vessels" may transit the Strait of Hormuz provided they coordinate with Iranian authorities, according to the Financial Times. Vessels linked to the United States, Israel, and what Tehran called "other participants in the aggression" are explicitly excluded from passage.

item.title: Prediction markets see Hormuz reopening unlikely before summer
item.description: Nearly four weeks after U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran triggered the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz, prediction markets and diplomatic signals suggest the world's most critical oil chokepoint will remain closed well into the summer, even as President Donald Trump claims negotiations with Tehran are underway.

item.title: Oil whipsaws as Trump's Hormuz deadline passes without action
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial shipping nearly a month after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the blockade, leaving global oil markets volatile and prediction markets signaling that disruptions could persist well into spring. Brent crude has surged roughly 55% from pre-war levels, while a draft UN Security Council resolution authorizing the use of force to reopen the waterway has introduced a new diplomatic front to the crisis.

item.title: Iran missiles hit Tel Aviv as US strikes kill PMF commander in Iraq
item.description: Iran launched multiple waves of missiles at Israel on Tuesday, striking central Tel Aviv and triggering sirens across the country, as a separate U.S. airstrike in western Iraq killed a senior commander of the Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces. The dual escalations came even as President Donald Trump claimed diplomatic progress with Tehran — assertions Iran dismissed as "false news."

item.title: Moldova declares 60-day energy emergency after Russian strikes sever key power line
item.description:
Moldova's parliament voted on Tuesday to impose a 60-day state of emergency in the country's energy sector after overnight Russian drone strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure severed the high-voltage Isaccea-Vulcănești power line, the primary conduit for electricity imports from Romania.

Seventy-two lawmakers in the 101-seat legislature approved the measure, with no votes against and 18 abstentions, according to the Associated Press. The emergency is set to take effect on Wednesday, March 25.

item.title: Israel renews Beirut bombardment, killing 3 including child
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in the town of Bchamoun, about 10 kilometers southeast of central Beirut, killed at least three people including a three-year-old girl early Tuesday, Lebanon's Health Ministry said. Five others were wounded in the predawn attack, which came as Israel renewed its bombardment of the Lebanese capital after a two-day lull.

Online footage showed flames engulfing at least one apartment in the struck building. The attack on Bchamoun, located in the Aley district of Mount Lebanon, hit outside the southern suburbs of Beirut where Israel had previously ordered evacuations and concentrated its strikes against Hezbollah.

item.title: Hezbollah's missile stockpile down to one-sixth of pre-war levels, Israel says
item.description:
Israel's military estimates that Hezbollah now possesses between 11,000 and 13,000 missiles and rockets, a sharp reduction to roughly one-sixth of the arsenal the Iranian-backed group held before October 2023, according to The Wall Street Journal. CNN separately confirmed the figures, reporting that the group's stockpile has been depleted after years of sustained Israeli strikes.

The assessment, provided by an Israeli military representative, represents a dramatic decline from the approximately 75,000 missiles and rockets Hezbollah was believed to possess before the Hamas-led attack on Israel in October 2023, according to estimates by the Alma Research and Education Center, an Israeli security think tank.

item.title: US sends Iran 15-point plan to end Middle East war
item.description: The United States has transmitted a 15-point plan to Iran aimed at ending the war in the Middle East, now in its fourth week, according to The New York Times, citing two officials briefed on the diplomacy. The proposal, delivered through Pakistan, outlines sweeping demands on Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile programs alongside provisions for the Strait of Hormuz, though it remains unclear whether Tehran views it as a viable basis for negotiations.

item.title: Saudi crown prince urges Trump to press for Iran regime's fall
item.description: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are taking concrete steps toward entering the month-old US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, as escalating Iranian attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure push longtime fence-sitters closer to open confrontation.

item.title: CENTCOM says 9,000 targets hit in Iran campaign's first 24 days
item.description: US Central Command announced on March 23 that Operation Epic Fury has struck more than 9,000 military targets inside Iran since the campaign began on February 28, marking one of the largest American military operations in the Middle East in decades. The updated fact sheet, published by the Department of Defense, also confirmed more than 9,000 combat flights and the destruction or damage of over 140 Iranian naval vessels across the first 24 days of the operation.

item.title: Second projectile hits Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant in a week
item.description:
A projectile struck the perimeter of Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant on Tuesday evening local time, the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran reported, marking the second such incident at the facility in just over a week. The strike, which occurred at approximately 9:08 p.m. local time on March 24, resulted in no casualties, damage, or disruption to operations, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.

The IAEA confirmed it had been informed by Iran of the latest projectile impact at the plant. Iran's atomic energy organization accused the United States and Israel of carrying out the attack.

item.title: Israel says it killed Quds Force operative in Beirut strike
item.description: The Israeli military and Shin Bet announced on Tuesday that they killed Muhammad Ali Kourani, described as a member of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force, in a naval strike on the Beirut area carried out the previous day. The Israeli Defense Forces said Kourani had been "advancing terror attacks directed by Iranian intelligence officials" from within Lebanon.

item.title: Iran fires cluster bomb missile at Bnei Brak, injuring 9
item.description:
Nine people, including six children, were injured on Tuesday after an Iranian ballistic missile carrying a cluster bomb warhead struck the central Israeli city of Bnei Brak, dispersing bomblets over a wide area that also reached nearby Petah Tikva. The attack was one of several Iranian missile barrages that struck Israeli cities throughout the day as the conflict between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition entered its fourth week.

Magen David Adom, Israel's emergency medical service, reported that a 23-year-old man was in moderate condition with shrapnel wounds, while eight others — including six children — sustained mild injuries from blast effects and shrapnel. Footage from the scene showed cluster submunitions scattered across residential areas, a weapon type Iran has repeatedly deployed against Israeli population centers during the war.

item.title: Iran stops all gas exports to Turkey after South Pars strike
item.description:
Iran has stopped all natural gas exports to Turkey following Israel's March 18 strike on the South Pars gas field, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The halt marks the latest energy disruption from an attack that has sent shockwaves through global markets and intensified a broader confrontation across the Middle East.

Turkey purchased approximately 14% of its natural gas from Iran last year, according to data from the Turkish Natural Gas Distributors Association cited by Bloomberg. According to Türkiye Today, roughly 75% of Iranian gas flows to Turkey had already been cut in the immediate aftermath of the strike before the full halt took effect. The Turkish Energy Ministry declined to comment on the situation.

item.title: Erdogan vows to keep Turkey out of Iran war's 'ring of fire'
item.description:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Tuesday vowed that Turkey would remain outside the widening conflict engulfing the Middle East, delivering a pointed rebuke of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and warning that the world's eight billion people are paying the price for what he called "Netanyahu's war for survival."

Speaking after a cabinet meeting in Ankara on the 25th day of the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, Erdogan said Turkey is "determined to keep our country out of this ring of fire" and rejected attempts by warring parties to draw Ankara into the conflict.

"We are not falling into traps set for us," Erdogan said, according to Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency. "The past 25 days have shown that while this is Israel's war, the world is paying the price."
